**STAT 5700 — Quiz 3**  
**Date:** February 26, 2026  

\textbf{\textcolor{red}{SOLUTIONS}}
\

Suppose you are a nurse working at a blood drive.  People with O- (“O-negative") blood type are coveted, because they are considered “universal donors”, meaning their blood can be donated to people of any blood type. About 8% of the population has type O-. Assume you have 50 donors and are interested in modeling how many are O-. Assume each donor's blood type is independent of the others'.  

a. What distribution is appropriate to model this scenario? Provide the name of the distribution and the values of its parameter(s). 
\
$$
\textcolor{red}{
Binomial(n = 50, p = 0.08)
}
$$
\

b. Write out the probability distribution, $p(y)$, for this scenario. Make sure to include the support. 
\
$$
\textcolor{red}{
p(y) = \binom{50}{y} (0.08)^y(0.92)^{(50 - y)}, \ \ \ y = 0,1,\dots 50
}
$$
\

c. What is the probability that at least two of the 50 donors are O-?
\
\
$$
\textcolor{red}{
\begin{aligned}
P(Y\geq 2) &= 1 - P(Y = 0) - P(Y = 1) \\
&=1 - \binom{50}{0}(0.08)^0(0.92)^{50} - \binom{50}{1}(0.08)^1(0.92)^{49}\\
&= 0.917288
\end{aligned}
}
$$

\
d. What is the expected (average) number of O- donors among the 50? 

$$
\textcolor{red}{
E(Y) = np = 50(0.08) = 4
}
$$
